clue.text: I love going to island cricket club for lively music

parts.note: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples
love is nil in tennis scoring, the round letter O

explanation.surface: Someone happily heads off to an island cricket club where lively music is played.
explanation.walkthrough: In answer order the island and the club come first, then I and O tagged on.
explanation.definitionFit: A capriccio is a free, lively piece of music in no strict form.

clue.text: Copper coin — two such might have been in the yard

definitions.text: two such might have been in the yard

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a bit is a small coin, as in a threepenny bit

explanation.surface: A copper coin lies in the yard, perhaps with another beside it.
explanation.walkthrough: A yard (36 inches) is roughly two of the old 18-inch measure; 'yard' looks like a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A cubit was an ancient length, about eighteen inches, from elbow to fingertip.

clue.text: Word Johnson misdefined, making the old man severe

parts.note: the old man is slang for father, PA
stern means severe

explanation.surface: Dr Johnson's error makes his old man stern.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Johnson's Dictionary called this part of a horse's leg its knee, an error he put down to 'ignorance, madam, pure ignorance'. 'making' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The pastern is the part of a horse's foot between fetlock and hoof, which Johnson famously got wrong.

clue.text: The sort of licensee Minnie is?

definitions.text: The sort of licensee Minnie is?

parts.words: The sort of licensee Minnie is?
parts.note: the name Minnie holds the word for a pub inside its first and last letters, so it keeps a pub

explanation.definitionFit: A publican running an inn holds the licence to sell drink there.

clue.text: Horse to go over, somersaulting

indicators.note: a somersault turns something head over heels, so the word for going over is read backwards

parts.note: to recap is to go over the main points again

explanation.surface: A horse is set to go over a jump but somersaults instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somersaulting' turns RECAP round.
explanation.definitionFit: A pacer is a horse that moves both legs on one side together, used in harness racing.

clue.text: Fairy on lake constitutes a danger

parts.note: a peri is a fairy of Persian legend
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A fairy standing on a lake puts herself in danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' and 'constitutes' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Peril means serious danger.

clue.text: Seen in plumage, finally tell it is a bird!

indicators.note: seen in places the picked letter inside the plumage word

parts.note: a bird's plumage is its coat

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the next word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Spotted in its feathers, one finally announces it is a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The coal tit is a small black-capped bird of the tit family.

clue.text: Compensated when garment gets covered in grass

indicators.note: the garment is covered by the grass word, sitting inside it

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
a dress is a garment

explanation.surface: A garment is left out on the grass and gets covered in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To redress a wrong is to make amends for it, so redressed means made up for.

clue.text: Cricketer goes around without helmet

indicators.note: the cricketer's word surrounds the other piece, as one thing going around another

parts.note: a bat is a batsman, a cricketer who bats
sine is Latin for without, as in sine die

explanation.surface: A batsman walks out to the crease without his helmet.
explanation.walkthrough: SINE, Latin for 'without', is a convention worth knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: A basinet is a light medieval steel headpiece, a kind of armoured headgear.

clue.text: Fabulous female makes me jolly — help!

parts.note: taken as written
a jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM
aid means help

explanation.surface: Someone cries that a jolly mood has struck and calls for help.
explanation.walkthrough: JOLLY as a Royal Marine (RM) is a crossword convention; 'makes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A mermaid is a creature of fable, so she is literally a fabulous female.

clue.text: In that respect, please feel reassured!

definitions.meaning: as in '... I disagree', meaning on that point
the soothing cry '..., ...' used to comfort someone

explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means 'on that point', and repeated it is a word of comfort to someone upset.

clue.text: After half a month character almost finished short book

indicators.note: the letter piece is placed after the month piece
only the first half of the month's name is kept

parts.note: November is a month

indicators.note: almost finished means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a character is a letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Halfway through a month, a character nearly finishes writing a short book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half a' leaves NOVE from NOVEMBER; 'almost finished' cuts LETTER to LETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A novelette is a short novel, often a slight or sentimental one.

clue.text: Freely offered tender love, circulating around university

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the other piece
circulating sends the letters round into a new order

explanation.surface: Tender love circulates around a university campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circulating' is the anagram signal for the first two words, and 'around' sends that mix round the university letter, which sits in the second position.
explanation.definitionFit: To volunteer something is to offer it of your own free will.

clue.text: Ladder? Bit of it's not good

indicators.note: not says the letter for good is to be left out

parts.note: a rung is a bit of a ladder, the 'it' of the clue

explanation.surface: A ladder is shown with a broken bit that is no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ladder' suggests climbing, but it is the run in a stocking; 'it' points back to the ladder whose rung loses G.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladder in tights is a run, a line where the stitches have come undone.

clue.text: Once again put in to control unit in mart

parts.note: to rein in is to control
a stall is one trader's unit in a market

explanation.surface: Someone is put back in charge of a unit in a market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once again put in' means installed a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinstall is to install, or put in, again.

clue.text: Players getting excited about wicket? That may be experienced after 'death rattle'

definitions.text: That may be experienced after 'death rattle'

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go about the other piece
excited players are stirred up, so their letters are mixed up

parts.note: a wicket is a small gate, as in wicket gate

explanation.surface: Cricketers get worked up over the fall of a wicket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' mixes the players' letters, and 'about' wraps them round the wicket, a cricket word that here means a small gate, breaking in just before the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: The pearly gates are the gates of heaven, which the dead are said to reach after their last breath.

clue.text: Approaches the snooker table but loses form

definitions.meaning: a player goes to the table to pot a ball

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to go to ruin, and literally describes going up to pot a ball.

clue.text: Someone who's succeeded must have got it

definitions.text: Someone who's succeeded must have got it

parts.words: Someone who's succeeded must have got it
parts.note: succeeded reads as achieved success but means followed an earlier holder of an estate or title

explanation.definitionFit: An heir succeeds to property, and what passes to that successor is the legacy received.

clue.text: Wartime precautions in house covering possible missile

indicators.note: in puts the precautions inside the house abbreviation

parts.note: ARP was Air Raid Precautions, the British wartime civil defence service
covering is on, as a lid is on a pot

explanation.surface: Wartime precautions in a house provide cover from a possible missile.
explanation.walkthrough: ARP (Air Raid Precautions) was Britain's Second World War civil defence organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: A harpoon is a barbed spear thrown or fired at whales, a missile of sorts.

clue.text: Passionate interest dying away, not half

indicators.note: not half means half the word is dropped, leaving its first three letters

parts.note: the clue's phrase means growing fainter and disappearing

explanation.surface: A passion fades away until it is not even half what it was.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' strips ING from FADING.
explanation.definitionFit: A fad is a craze, an intense but short-lived enthusiasm.

clue.text: Sweet, weakly indulgent little creature

parts.note: fond in its sense of foolishly doting
an ant is a little creature

explanation.surface: A sweet, softly doting little animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A fondant is a soft creamy sweet made from sugar.

clue.text: Sudden increase to cover cleaner's addition to bill

indicators.note: the surge wraps round the other piece, covering it

parts.note: a surge is a sudden increase
a char is a cleaning woman, a charwoman

explanation.surface: A sudden pay rise for the cleaner is added to the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAR is British for a cleaning woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A surcharge is an extra charge added on to the usual price.

clue.text: Cry of encouragement when country dance is announced?

indicators.note: announced means spoken, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: the hay is an old country dance with interweaving lines

explanation.surface: A cry of encouragement goes up when the country dance is called.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Heigh is an old exclamation used to cheer on or encourage, as in heigh-ho.

clue.text: Arrangement of nonet for Mass

explanation.surface: A musical arrangement for nine players is performed at Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' reads as a church service but is weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonne is a metric unit of mass, a thousand kilograms.

clue.text: Philosopher, a follower of Aquinas wasting hours

indicators.note: wasting means losing the letter for hours

parts.note: a Thomist follows the teachings of Thomas Aquinas

explanation.surface: A philosopher is a disciple of Aquinas who wastes his hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasting' takes H from THOMIST.
explanation.definitionFit: An atomist is a philosopher holding that everything is made of tiny indivisible particles, like Democritus.

clue.text: Little fellow stopping the enemy short

indicators.note: short means cut, losing the last letter

parts.note: time is called the enemy, as in 'how goes the enemy?'

explanation.surface: A small man holds back the enemy, though he falls short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the enemy' for TIME is an old crossword convention; Tiny Tim is the little fellow of Dickens's A Christmas Carol.

clue.text: Artist to help a struggling painter

explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' makes PHAEL from HELP A; 'to' is a link.

explanation.definitionFit: Lunch is the midday meal.

clue.text: Thinks that could be estimated

explanation.definitionFit: To meditate is to think deeply and quietly about something.
